paragraphs: Rav Yitzchak the son of Rav.

Yuchasin and Seder HaDorot mention him without giving a citation. There is indeed such a reading in the Rif and Rosh on Moed Katan 17b: “What is tavra? Rav Yitzchak son of Rav said…” But a manuscript of the Rif correctly reads Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehudah, as cited in Dikdukei Soferim.

As for Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:1, with the additional historical folio locator 2b, which has Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rav, Hyman explained under Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Chiyya Kahuna that the reading should be son of Rabbi Chiyya Kahuna there.

notes.text: Hyman proposes Rav Yehudah for the first father-name and Chiyya Kahuna for the second. The two claims are preserved without identifying every abbreviated Rav as the same person.
The supplied Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot locator is chapter 3, halakhah 1, with the additional folio locator ב:, rendered 2b. It is not a range of halakhot 1–2.

The consulted Bavli Moed Katan 17b reads Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehudah. This is distinct from inspecting the particular Rif, Rosh or manuscript cited by Hyman; their exact readings and his Chiyya Kahuna correction remain attributed to him.
